info.title: Kaspi Cashier API
info.description:
Accept Kaspi Pay payments on your own site or app: create a payment, get a payment link/QR code, and track payment status — without integrating with the bank directly. This is not an official Kaspi merchant API — the integration works the same way the Kaspi Pay Cashier mobile app does. We maintain compatibility and will notify you if Kaspi changes their side.

## Quick start
1. **Connect the Cashier role** — on the `/kaspi-api` page, enter the phone number that already has the Kaspi Pay app's "Cashier" role, and confirm the SMS code.
2. **Save your API token and webhook secret** — right after connecting, two values are shown once: an API token (for API requests) and a separate webhook secret (for verifying webhook signatures, see the Webhooks section below). Copy and save both — they are not shown again (you can only disconnect Cashier and reconnect it, which issues new ones).
3. **Hand them to your developer or wire them into your site** — if you're not building the site yourself, send these two values and a link to this page to your developer.
4. **Create a payment** — send the request from the `POST /api/kaspi/pay` example below with an amount and your own order id. The response contains a link/QR — show it to the customer.
5. **Learn about the payment automatically** — the simplest way is to poll the status endpoint (`GET /api/kaspi/pay/status`) while the customer is on the payment page, or set up a webhook instead (see the Webhooks section below).

## Pricing
Connecting and accepting payments is free on any plan. A 2% commission is debited from your wallet balance only for confirmed payments — e.g. a ₸10,000 payment debits ₸200. Top up your balance in advance on the `/kaspi-api` page.

servers.description: Production — the only environment; there is no test/sandbox mode

tags.name: Kaspi Cashier API
tags.description: Accepting and tracking Kaspi Pay payments

bearerAuth.description: Your Kaspi Cashier connection's API token. Issued once on the /kaspi-api page when you connect the "Cashier" role — save it immediately, it is not shown again (if it's lost or leaked, disconnect and reconnect Cashier to get a new one). It belongs only to your connection — never reused by anyone else.

order_id.description: A unique order identifier on your side

callback_url.description: Your webhook URL for the payment-success notification. Must start with https:// and must not point at localhost or a private network (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x) — otherwise the webhook is simply not sent.

qr_token.description: Token used to render the payment's QR code

payment_link.description: Payment link — can be handed to the customer directly

operation_id.description: Unique operation id on Kaspi's side

expire_date.description: Date and time the QR code expires

status.description: pending — awaiting payment, paid — paid, expired — the QR code expired unpaid

required.description: The commission amount (2% of amount) your balance needs to cover

balance.description: Your current wallet balance in tenge

error.description: kaspi_unavailable — the request to Kaspi itself failed; tracking_failed — the payment was created on Kaspi's side but we failed to save it for tracking on ours (rare) — contact support
A failure talking to Kaspi while checking the status

post.description: Creates a Kaspi Pay payment and returns a link/QR for the customer. Limit: 20 requests per 60 seconds per connection. A 2% commission is debited from your wallet balance only once the payment is confirmed.

400.description: Bad Request — a required field is missing

401.description: Unauthorized — the token is missing or invalid

402.description: Payment Required — insufficient wallet balance to cover the commission; top up on the /kaspi-api page

429.description: Too Many Requests — the 20-requests-per-minute-per-connection limit was exceeded

502.description: Bad Gateway — a failure talking to Kaspi, or the payment was created but couldn't be saved for tracking

get.description: Every call genuinely re-checks the status with Kaspi (it does not just read our database) — safe to poll every few seconds while the customer waits on the payment page.

parameters.name: operation_id
parameters.description: The operation_id returned when the payment was created

400.description: Bad Request — operation_id was not provided

401.description: Unauthorized — the token is missing or invalid

404.description: Not Found — no payment with that operation_id exists

502.description: Bad Gateway — a failure talking to Kaspi

post.description: If a callback_url was provided when creating the payment, invoices.kz sends it a POST request the moment the payment is confirmed. Signed with an X-Kaspi-Pay-Signature header (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with your webhook secret). The webhook secret is unique per connection — other invoices.kz customers' webhooks are signed with a different key, and vice versa. This is not the only signal of payment — it fires either when you call GET /api/kaspi/pay/status yourself, or when our internal cron discovers the payment (that cron runs once a day).

parameters.name: X-Kaspi-Pay-Signature
parameters.description: hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the raw JSON body, signed with this connection's webhook secret

200.description: Acknowledged — return 200 once the webhook has been processed successfully
